research_mode: official Office for National Statistics sources only; year-ending March 2026 CSEW fieldwork, reference period, redesigned sensitive measures, deferred quality assurance and uncertainty; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Year-ending March 2026 CSEW interview window
verified_claims: the year-ending March 2026 CSEW is based on interviews from April 2025 to March 2026
the interview window is distinct from the crime occurrence window
the release tracks the series through March 2026
limitations: interview month is not incident month
annual estimates combine overlapping recall periods

sources.name: Year-ending March 2026 crime occurrence window
verified_claims: the latest CSEW figures cover crimes occurring between April 2024 and February 2026
the occurrence period reflects the 12-month recall design across interviews
the occurrence window is wider than a single calendar year
limitations: the window must not be labelled as a single incident year
survey recall timing differs from police record dates

sources.name: Current CSEW violence estimate
verified_claims: the year-ending March 2026 CSEW estimated 989,000 incidents of violence with or without injury
the estimate covers people aged 16 years and over
the figure is a survey estimate rather than a count of police records
limitations: the national estimate is not a parcel-level rate
sampling uncertainty applies

sources.name: Current violence trend significance
verified_claims: ONS reports no statistically significant change in violence with or without injury from the previous survey year
the conclusion is based on survey uncertainty
the release separately reports long-term reductions
limitations: no significant change is not proof of zero change
national significance does not describe every subgroup or locality

sources.name: Redeveloped sexual-victimisation questions
verified_claims: CSEW questions on sexual victimisation were redeveloped
the purpose was to improve measurement
the latest estimates use the redeveloped questions
limitations: questionnaire improvement can create a series break
measure version must accompany every estimate

sources.name: Sexual-victimisation series comparability
verified_claims: ONS states the latest sexual-victimisation estimates are not comparable with previously published measures
the noncomparability follows questionnaire redevelopment
trend claims across the break are therefore unsupported
limitations: new and old estimates must not be joined into a continuous trend
no adjustment is implied by the release

sources.name: Deferred domestic-abuse and stalking estimates
verified_claims: year-ending March 2026 domestic-abuse and stalking estimates will be released separately later in 2026
ONS is taking additional time for quality assurance
further analysis is also being completed before publication
limitations: deferred estimates must not be inferred from other series
absence at release time is not a zero value

sources.name: Deferred combined sensitive-crime measure
verified_claims: the combined measure of domestic abuse sexual victimisation and stalking will be available later in 2026
the delay follows the separate timing of component estimates
the current release does not contain the updated combined value
limitations: the previous combined estimate must not be relabelled as March 2026
component delays prevent current recomputation

sources.name: Sensitive measures outside CSEW headline crime
verified_claims: domestic abuse sexual victimisation stalking and harassment are not included in CSEW headline crime figures
these topics are reported separately
the separation reflects questionnaire and measurement design
limitations: headline crime must not be treated as all victimisation
separately reported measures use different denominators and versions

sources.name: CSEW sampling uncertainty boundary
verified_claims: the CSEW uses a sample rather than the whole population
survey estimates therefore have uncertainty
ONS states that estimates are not precise population counts
limitations: point estimates require confidence and significance context
sampling uncertainty is not the only possible survey error
